source_text:
Πῶς γὰρ Πέτρος τὸν Ἀνανίαν καὶ τὴν Σαπφείραν ἤλεγξε νοσφισαμένους ἐκ τῆς τιμῆς τοῦ χωρίου, εἰ
μὴ χάρισμα προφητείας εἶχε; Πῶς δὲ καὶ ὁ ἅγιος Παῦλος ἔλεγε τὰ μέλλοντα ἐπ' ἐσχάτου τῶν ἡμερῶν ἔσεσθαι, εἰ μὴ καὶ αὐτὸς εἶχεν χάρισμα προφητείας; {Μ.} Πῶς οὖν οὐ δέχεσθε Μοντανὸν τὸν ἅγιον; {Ο.} Ὅτι ψευδοπροφήτης ἦν οὐδὲν ἀληθὲς λέγων. {Μ.} Μὴ βλασφήμει, ἄνθρωπε, τὸν παράκλητον. {Ο.} Ἐγὼ αἰνῶ καὶ δοξάζω τὸν παράκλητον, τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς ἀληθείας, Μοντανὸν δὲ βδελύσσομαι ὡς τὸ βδέλυγμα τῆς ἐρημώσεως. {Μ.} Πῶς; {Ο.} Πρῶτον, ὅτι λέγει· Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ πατὴρ καὶ ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ υἱὸς καὶ ἐγὼ ὁ παράκλητος. {Μ.} Ὑμεῖς δὲ λέγετε, ὅτι· Ἄλλος ἐστὶν ὁ πατὴρ καὶ ἄλλος ὁ υἱὸς καὶ ἄλλο τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον. {Ο.} Ἐὰν ἡμεῖς λέγωμεν, οὐδὲν ἀξιόπιστον· ἐὰν δὲ ὁ υἱὸς διδάσκῃ, ἄλλον εἶναι τὸν πατέρα καὶ ἄλλον τὸν παράκλητον, τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, ἀνάγκη πείθεσθαι. {Μ.} ∆εῖξον, ποῦ διδάσκει. {Ο.} Ὅταν λέγῃ· Ἐγὼ ἐρωτήσω τὸν πατέρα, καὶ ἄλλον παράκλητον δώσει ὑμῖν, τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς ἀληθείας, ἵνα ᾖ μεθ' ὑμῶν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, ὃ ὁ κόσμος οὐ δύναται λαβεῖν, ὅτι οὐ θεωρεῖ αὐτό· ὑμεῖς δὲ γιγνώσκετε, ὅτι παρ' ὑμῖν μένει καὶ ἐν ὑμῖν ἔσται. Πῶς οὐχὶ φανερῶς ἄλλον παράκλητον ἀκούων ἄλλον παρ' αὐτὸν τὸν λέγοντα νοεῖς; {Μ.} Εἰ ἄλλος καὶ ἄλλος καὶ ἄλλος, τρεῖς θεοί. {Ο.} Μὴ γένοιτο. {Μ.} Πῶς· μὴ γένοιτο; {Ο.} Ὅτι ἡ θεία γραφὴ τὰ τὴν αὐτὴν ἔχοντα φύσιν καὶ βουλὴν ἑνοῖ. {Μ.} Μὴ γένοιτο. {Ο.} Ἀκούεις Παύλου τοῦ ἀποστόλου λέγοντος, ὅτι· Ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ οὐκ ἔνι δοῦλος οὐδὲ ἐλεύθερος· οὐκ ἔνι ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ· οὐκ ἔνι Ἕλλην καὶ Ἰουδαῖος, 453 ἀλλὰ πάντες ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ εἷς ἐστε. Καὶ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἀκούομεν λέγοντος περὶ τοῦ ἀνδρὸς καὶ τῆς γυναικός, ὅτι οὐκέτι εἰσὶ δύο, ἀλλὰ σὰρξ μία. Εἰ δὲ τὰ ἐν διαστάσει ὄντα οὐκέτι εἰσὶ δύο διὰ τὸ ταὐτὸν τῆς βουλῆς καὶ τῆς φύσεως, πῶς δυνατὸν τὰ ἀσώματα ὑπὸ ἀριθμὸν καὶ θέσιν γενέσθαι; {Μ.} Οὐκ ἔστιν οὖν εἷς θεός. {Ο.} Εἷς θεὸς τῷ λόγῳ τῆς φύσεως, τῇ δὲ ὑποστάσει ἄλλος ἐστὶν ὁ πατὴρ καὶ ἄλλος ὁ υἱὸς καὶ ἄλλος τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον. {Μ.} Πῶς οὖν ὁ υἱὸς λέγει· Ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ γνώσονται, ὅτι ἐγὼ ἐν τῷ πατρὶ καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ἐν ἐμοί; Καὶ πάλιν λέγει· Ἄν τις ἀγαπᾷ με, τὸν λόγον μου τηρήσει, καὶ ὁ πατήρ μου τηρήσει αὐτόν, καὶ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐλευσόμεθα καὶ μονὴν παρ' αὐτῷ ποιησόμεθα. Ὁ μὴ ἀγαπῶν με τοὺς λόγους μου οὐ τηρεῖ καὶ ὁ λόγος ὁ ἐμὸς οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμός, ἀλλὰ τοῦ πέμψαντός με. Ταῦτα λελάληκα ὑμῖν παρ' ὑμῖν μένων· ὁ δὲ παράκλητος, τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, ὃ πέμψει ὁ πατὴρ ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου, ἐκεῖνο ὑμᾶς διδάξει πάντα καὶ ὑπομνήσει πάντα, ἃ εἶπον ἐγώ. {Ο.} Ἄκων συναινεῖς τῷ λόγῳ τῆς ἀληθείας. Εἰ γὰρ πείθῃ τοῖς εἰρημένοις, ὀρθοποδήσεις πρὸς τὴν ἀλήθειαν. Ἤκουσας, ὅτι λέγει· Ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ γνώσεσθε, ὅτι ἐγὼ ἐν τῷ πατρὶ καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ἐν ἐμοί, καὶ οὐκ εἶπεν· Ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ γνώσεσθε πάντες, ὅτι ἐγὼ πατὴρ καὶ υἱός εἰμι. Ἀκούεις δέ, ὅτι λέγει· καὶ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐλευσόμεθα ἐγὼ καὶ ὁ πατήρ· οὐκ εἶπε πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἐλεύσομαι ἐγὼ καὶ ὁ πατὴρ καὶ ὁ υἱὸς καὶ μονὴν ποιήσω· ἀλλὰ καὶ τό· Ὁ λόγος ὁ ἐμὸς οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμός, ἀλλὰ τοῦ πέμψαντός με, οὐδὲν ἕτερον δηλοῖ ἢ τῶν ὑποστάσεων τὴν ἰδιότητα· καὶ ὅταν δέ· ταῦτα λελάληκα ὑμῖν παρ' ὑμῖν μένων, ἀκούσῃς, ὁ δὲ παράκλητος τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, ὃ πέμψει ὁ πατὴρ ἐν τῷ ἐμῷ ὀνόματι, ἐκεῖνος διδάξει ὑμᾶς πάντα, ἃ εἶπον ὑμῖν, πῶς οὐ σαυτὸν ἐρυθριάσας ὁμολογήσεις τῶν τριῶν ὑποστάσεων τὴν εὐκρίνειαν; 454 {Μ.} Ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ... κρίσεως αἱ τρεῖς ὑποστάσεις καθέζονται κρῖναι ζῶντας καὶ νεκρούς. {Ο.} Τὸ καθέζονται σωματικῶς ἀκούων πνευματικῶς νόει, ἵνα μὴ τόπους καὶ χωρισμοὺς σωμάτων ὑπολάβῃς, ἀλλὰ τὸ πάγιον τῆς φύσεως. Πανταχοῦ γὰρ ὁ πατήρ, πανταχοῦ ὁ υἱός, πανταχοῦ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, καὶ ὥσπερ οὐδὲν μέσον ἐστὶν νοῦ καὶ λόγου καὶ πνοῆς, οὕτως οὐδὲν μέσον πατρὸς καὶ υἱοῦ καὶ ἁγίου πνεύματος.
thought_title: The three persons are one God, not three gods
orientation: The Montanist has just objected that the Orthodox speaker's distinction of Father, Son, and Spirit implies three gods; the Orthodox speaker now argues from Scripture that the three share one nature and will, and that the Son himself teaches the distinction of persons.
pass_a_gloss: For how [did] Peter convict Ananias and Sapphira [when they had] embezzled from the price of the field, if he did not have [the] gift of prophecy? How also [did] holy Paul say the things about to be at [the] last of the days, if he also did not have [the] gift of prophecy? {M.} How then do you not accept Montanus the holy [one]? {O.} Because he was a false prophet saying nothing true. {M.} Do not blaspheme, man, the Advocate. {O.} I praise and glorify the Advocate, the Spirit of truth, but Montanus I abhor as the abomination of desolation. {M.} How? {O.} First, because he says: I am the Father and I am the Son and I [am] the Advocate. {M.} But you say that: Another is the Father and another the Son and another the Holy Spirit. {O.} If we say [it], [it is] nothing trustworthy; but if the Son teaches [that] another is the Father and another the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, [it is] necessary to be persuaded. {M.} Show where he teaches. {O.} When he says: I will ask the Father, and another Advocate he will give you, the Spirit of truth, so that he may be with you unto the age, whom the world cannot receive, because it does not see him; but you know [him], because he remains with you and will be in you. How [do you] not clearly hearing another Advocate [and] another besides him the [one] speaking understand? {M.} If another and another and another, three gods. {O.} May it not be. {M.} How: may it not be? {O.} Because the divine Scripture unites the [things] having the same nature and will. {M.} May it not be. {O.} You hear Paul the apostle saying that: In Christ Jesus there is not slave nor free; there is not male and female; there is not Greek and Jew, but all in Christ Jesus are one. And of Christ himself we hear saying about the man and the woman, that no longer are they two, but one flesh. But if the [things] being in separation no longer are two because of the sameness of will and nature, how [is it] possible [for] the bodiless [things] to come under number and position? {M.} There is not therefore one God. {O.} One God by the word of nature, but in person another is the Father and another the Son and another the Holy Spirit. {M.} How then [does] the Son say: In that day they will know that I [am] in the Father and the Father in me? And again he says: If anyone loves me, my word he will keep, and my Father will keep him, and to him we will come and a dwelling with him we will make. The [one] not loving me my words does not keep and the word that is mine is not mine, but of the [one] having sent me. These things I have spoken to you remaining with you; but the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, that [one] will teach you all things and will remind [you of] all things that I said. {O.} Unwillingly you agree with the word of truth. For if you are persuaded by the things said, you will walk straight toward the truth. You heard that he says: In that day you will know that I [am] in the Father and the Father in me, and he did not say: In that day you will all know that I am Father and Son. But you hear that he says: and to him we will come, I and the Father; he did not say to him: I will come, I and the Father and the Son, and a dwelling I will make; but also the [saying]: The word that is mine is not mine, but of the [one] having sent me, indicates nothing other than the distinctness of the persons; and when [you hear]: these things I have spoken to you remaining with you, but the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, that [one] will teach you all things that I said to you, how [will you] not, having made yourself blush, confess the clear distinction of the three persons? {M.} In [the] day ... of judgment the three persons sit to judge [the] living and [the] dead. {O.} Hearing the [word] 'they sit' bodily, understand spiritually, so that you do not suppose places and separations of bodies, but the fixedness of the nature. For everywhere [is] the Father, everywhere the Son, everywhere the Holy Spirit, and just as nothing [is] between mind and word and breath, so nothing [is] between Father and Son and Holy Spirit.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'Advocate' for the Holy Spirit, avoiding 'Comforter', 'Helper', and 'Paraclete'.
The glossary requires 'person' for the distinct personal reality of Father, Son, and Spirit, avoiding 'hypostasis' and 'subsistence'.
Rendered literally to preserve the Johannine phrase, which the dialogue treats as a title of the Advocate.
The standard English rendering of the biblical phrase, which the Orthodox speaker applies to Montanus.
The Orthodox speaker quotes Paul's words to show that those sharing one nature and will are called one, supporting his argument against three gods.
The Orthodox speaker contrasts bodily sitting with the unchanging, non-spatial character of the divine nature; 'fixedness' preserves the sense of stability without implying physical location.

pass_b_english: How could Peter have exposed Ananias and Sapphira for embezzling from the price of the field unless he had the gift of prophecy? And how could Saint Paul have spoken of what would happen in the last days unless he too had the gift of prophecy? The Montanist said: "Then why do you not accept holy Montanus?" The Orthodox Christian said: "Because he was a false prophet who spoke nothing true." The Montanist said: "Do not blaspheme the Advocate, man." The Orthodox Christian said: "I praise and glorify the Advocate, the Spirit of truth, but I abhor Montanus as the abomination of desolation." The Montanist said: "How?" The Orthodox Christian said: "First, because he says: 'I am the Father and I am the Son and I am the Advocate.'" The Montanist said: "But you say that the Father is one, the Son is another, and the Holy Spirit is another." The Orthodox Christian said: "If we say it, it is not trustworthy; but if the Son teaches that the Father is one and the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, is another, then it is necessary to be persuaded." The Montanist said: "Show where he teaches this." The Orthodox Christian said: "When he says: 'I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Advocate, the Spirit of truth, to be with you forever, whom the world cannot receive because it does not see him; but you know him, because he remains with you and will be in you' (John 14:16-17). When you hear 'another Advocate,' how do you not clearly understand that he is another besides the one who speaks?" The Montanist said: "If one and another and another, then three gods." The Orthodox Christian said: "God forbid." The Montanist said: "How 'God forbid'?" The Orthodox Christian said: "Because the divine Scripture unites things that have the same nature and will." The Montanist said: "God forbid." The Orthodox Christian said: "You hear the apostle Paul saying: 'In Christ Jesus there is neither slave nor free; there is neither male nor female; there is neither Greek nor Jew, but you are all one in Christ Jesus' (Galatians 3:28). And we hear Christ himself saying about the man and the woman: 'They are no longer two, but one flesh' (Matthew 19:6). If things that exist in separation are no longer two because of the sameness of will and nature, how is it possible for bodiless things to come under number and position?" The Montanist said: "Then there is not one God." The Orthodox Christian said: "One God in respect of nature, but in person the Father is one, the Son is another, and the Holy Spirit is another." The Montanist said: "Then how does the Son say: 'On that day they will know that I am in the Father and the Father is in me' (John 14:20)? And again he says: 'If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will keep him, and we will come to him and make our dwelling with him. The one who does not love me does not keep my words, and the word that I speak is not mine, but the Father's who sent me' (John 14:23-24). 'These things I have spoken to you while remaining with you; but the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things and remind you of all that I have said to you' (John 14:25-26)." The Orthodox Christian said: "Unwillingly you agree with the word of truth. For if you are persuaded by what has been said, you will walk straight toward the truth. You heard that he says: 'On that day you will know that I am in the Father and the Father is in me,' and he did not say: 'On that day you will all know that I am Father and Son.' And you hear that he says: 'We will come to him, I and the Father'; he did not say to him: 'I and the Father and the Son will come and make a dwelling.' But also: 'The word that I speak is not mine, but the Father's who sent me' shows nothing other than the distinctness of the persons. And when you hear: 'These things I have spoken to you while remaining with you; but the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all that I have said to you,' how will you not, blushing at yourself, confess the clear distinction of the three persons?" The Montanist said: "On the day ... of judgment the three persons will sit to judge the living and the dead." The Orthodox Christian said: "When you hear 'they will sit' in a bodily way, understand it spiritually, so that you do not suppose places and separations of bodies, but the fixedness of the nature. For the Father is everywhere, the Son is everywhere, the Holy Spirit is everywhere, and just as there is nothing between mind and word and breath, so there is nothing between Father and Son and Holy Spirit."
notes: The source contains a lacuna in the Montanist's line: 'Ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ... κρίσεως' (In [the] day ... of judgment). The gloss marks the gap with ellipsis and does not supply missing text.

problems.quote: the Father is one, the Son is another, and the Holy Spirit is another.
problems.source_quote: Ἄλλος ἐστὶν ὁ πατὴρ καὶ ἄλλος ὁ υἱὸς καὶ ἄλλο τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον.
problems.why: Greek says each person is “another,” not “one,” reversing the theological claim.
problems.fix: the Father is another, the Son is another, and the Holy Spirit is another.

problems.quote: On the day of judgment the three persons will sit to judge the living and the dead.
problems.source_quote: Ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ... κρίσεως αἱ τρεῖς ὑποστάσεις καθέζονται κρῖναι ζῶντας καὶ νεκρούς.
problems.why: The source has a gap (marked by ...) in the text, but the English fills it in smoothly without indicating the lacuna. The reader cannot tell part of the source is missing.
problems.fix: On the day ... of judgment the three persons will sit to judge the living and the dead.
problems.ruling: Source shows ellipsis indicating missing text; English renders as complete sentence, hiding the lacuna.
